name: Dacono
title: Artificial Turf in Dacono, CO — Clay & Small Lots | NoCo Turf Co.
description: Dacono won't count synthetic turf toward required landscaping, its lots run small, and nearly half the ground is Weld loam. What that means for a yard.
h1: Dacono won't count synthetic turf toward the landscaping its code requires
lede: Dacono's code lets turf onto a house lot but won't count it as required landscaping, nearly half of the town's central ground is high shrink-swell Weld loam, and its median house lot is about 6,218 square feet.

answer.question: Can artificial turf count toward Dacono's landscaping requirements?
answer.answer: No. NoCo Turf Co. installs artificial turf in Dacono, Colorado, where the municipal code says synthetic turf can't meet its landscaping requirements. That is not an outright ban: on a house lot turf can go in, but required landscaping has to be met with something else. State law separately bars nonfunctional turf in new commercial and HOA common landscapes.

blocks.h2: Turf can go on a Dacono house lot, but it never counts as required landscaping.
paras: Dacono Municipal Code 16-657(g), from Ordinance No. 787 in 2014, says artificial plants and synthetic turfs may not be used to meet the requirements of the city's landscaping article.
Where a Dacono project has a required landscape area, plan the plants for that area first and put turf on the rest of the yard.

blocks.h2: Nearly half of central Dacono is Weld loam, a high shrink-swell soil.
paras: Soil surveys around central Dacono map Weld loam over nearly half of the area sampled, and NRCS rates the Weld series as limited for building because of shrink-swell.

The Colorado Geological Survey lists irrigation water soaking into the soil next to foundations among the landscaping problems on expansive ground, so a turf base in Dacono should shed water away from the house.
The largest hail NOAA logged near Dacono from 2011 through 2025 was 1.75 inches, on August 4, 2020.

blocks.h2: The median Dacono house lot is about 6,218 square feet.
paras: Glens at Dacono, the largest subdivision, has 758 lots with a median near 5,569 square feet; Sweetgrass, Sharpe and Autumn Valley Ranch follow. Eagle Meadow is the acreage exception, with a median lot near 26,894 square feet.
The state's district map puts 23 metro districts in Dacono, 11 formed in 2018 or later, and 10 of them belong to the Pinnacle Farms family.

blocks.h2: Dacono's water starts with Colorado-Big Thompson shares and a stake in NISP.
paras: Dacono's primary water source is Colorado-Big Thompson shares, it takes part in the Northern Integrated Supply Project, and it buys treated water from Central Weld County Water District. Northern Water set the 2026 C-BT quota at 0.8 acre-feet per unit.
The city has no mandatory watering restrictions in place and asks residents to use water efficiently.

faq.q: Can I turf my whole Dacono yard?
faq.a: Only the part that isn't required landscaping. Section 16-657(g) says synthetic turf can't meet the landscaping requirements, so ask the City what landscaping your lot must carry before you size the turf.

faq.q: Are there watering restrictions in Dacono in 2026?
faq.a: No mandatory ones. The City asks residents to use water efficiently and avoid unnecessary waste.
Much of it is. Weld loam, a high shrink-swell soil, covers nearly half of the area sampled around central Dacono.
